content: If you miss a dose of this medication, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. For storage, keep the unopened bottle in the refrigerator. Once opened, the bottle can be stored either in the refrigerator or at room temperature. However, once the bottle is opened, the medication expires after 14 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is important to note that this document is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Before using azithromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin or clarithromycin), or to ketolide antibiotics (such as telithromycin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. After applying this drug, your vision may become temporarily blurred. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if azithromycin passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, this medication may be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another condition unless directed by your doctor. Discard any unused medication after treatment is completed or after 14 days (refer to the storage section for details).
